info.title: econiq domain API
info.description:
Evidence-backed, Process-first investment research.

The chain every response can be walked back along:

    Documents → Claims → Events → Processes → States
    → Bottlenecks → Capabilities → Assets

Reads accept `as_of` to reconstruct the graph as it was at a past instant.
Scores are returned per family with their inputs attached — Thesis quality,
Asset quality and Trade quality are never combined.

get.description:
Readiness, including the migration the database is actually on.

The schema version matters: an API serving a database one migration behind
will fail in ways that look like data problems rather than deployment ones.

Processes ranked by how much their evidence has moved.

The filters are the screener of §25. They are applied *before* ranking where
they are cheap row predicates and after where they depend on the ranking's
own measurements, but either way the ordering within a filtered set is the
same ordering the unfiltered feed would give — a screener that reranked its
results would answer a different question from the one the user asked.

schema.title: Response State History Api Processes  Process Id  States Get

get.description:
State changes, belief changes, evidence and critiques on one axis (#20).

Three separate lists would leave the reader joining them by eye, and the
join is the point: a belief change is only defensible next to the evidence
that arrived just before it. The entries carry both dates — when the thing
happened and when the system learned it — because a document published in
July and ingested in August belongs in two different places depending on
which question is being asked.

if the attacks remain on the record.

Structural checks Postgres cannot express (issue #13).

need it, and because a graph that has quietly acquired a causal cycle should
be visible rather than discovered through a traversal that makes no sense.

AgentRunOut.title: AgentRunOut
AgentRunOut.description: The provenance record every derived row cites.

AssetClass.title: AssetClass
AssetClass.description:
Ontology §14. V1 expresses theses through the underlying asset only —
options and derivatives are explicitly out of scope.

discovery_chain.title: Discovery Chain
discovery_chain.description: Why this Asset is in the graph (issue #28).

AssetIdentifiersOut.title: AssetIdentifiersOut
AssetIdentifiersOut.description: Not equity-only: a commodity carries a code and a benchmark, a currency a pair.

BottleneckKind.title: BottleneckKind
BottleneckKind.description: Ontology §11 — what class of constraint blocks the Process.

currently_binding.title: Currently Binding
currently_binding.description: Whether it constrains the Process now, or would only later.

upstream_processes.title: Upstream Processes
upstream_processes.description: Processes reaching this Capability. Several independent ones is confluence (ontology §13), read off the graph rather than asserted.

source_location.title: Source Location
source_location.description: Verified span: the quote and its offsets in the parsed document.

CritiqueKind.title: CritiqueKind
CritiqueKind.description:
The seven lines of attack the Process Critic must take (agent doc §6.5).

A closed vocabulary because the critic's coverage is measurable: an
adversarial pass that only ever finds "contradictory evidence" is not
attacking the thesis from seven directions.

CritiqueStatus.title: CritiqueStatus
CritiqueStatus.description:
What became of a critique.

Critiques are never deleted. A thesis that survived an attack is stronger
than one that was never attacked, and that is only visible if the attacks
remain on the record.

Direction.title: Direction
Direction.description:
Which way to walk the typed edges.

The canonical chain runs Process → Bottleneck → Capability → Asset, so
``DOWNSTREAM`` answers "what could express this Process" and ``UPSTREAM``
answers "why is this Asset here" — the two questions the UI asks most.

is_prediction.title: Is Prediction
is_prediction.description: A discovery ranking, not a forecast (ui_concept §5.2). Present so a client cannot mistake the ordering for a predicted return.

DiscoverFeedOut.title: DiscoverFeedOut
DiscoverFeedOut.description:
The Discover feed, with its own limits attached.

``unavailable_inputs`` is part of the response rather than documentation: a
ranking that silently drops half of its stated inputs is a different ranking
wearing the same name, and the screen should be able to say so.

DiscoveryPathOut.title: DiscoveryPathOut
DiscoveryPathOut.description: One route from a Process down to an Asset, with the reason at each step.

evidence_recent.title: Evidence Recent
evidence_recent.description: Evidence links in the trailing window.

evidence_prior.title: Evidence Prior
evidence_prior.description: The window before it, for comparison.

contradiction_count.title: Contradiction Count
contradiction_count.description: Evidence recorded against this Process. Shown rather than netted off: contradiction is a scored dimension, not a deduction (§17).

source_breadth.title: Source Breadth
source_breadth.description: Distinct publishers behind the supporting Events. A media-coverage proxy, reported beside the rank rather than inside it — Phase 0 has no market data, and calling this 'attention' would make §5.2's central claim untestable.

EmergingProcessOut.title: EmergingProcessOut
EmergingProcessOut.description: A row of the emerging-Process panel (§5.1).

EntityType.title: EntityType
EntityType.description:
Node types in the economic graph.

Mirrors the top-level ontology chain (ontology §3). Every node registered in
the graph declares one of these, which is what makes typed edges checkable.

independent_source_count.title: Independent Source Count
independent_source_count.description: Distinct reports behind this Event after syndication collapse — not the document count (ontology §47).

propagated_at.title: Propagated At
propagated_at.description: When this Event cleared the significance gate. Null means it is accumulating.

independent_source_count.title: Independent Source Count
independent_source_count.description: Distinct reports behind this Event after syndication collapse — not the document count (ontology §47).

propagated_at.title: Propagated At
propagated_at.description: When this Event cleared the significance gate. Null means it is accumulating.

EventType.title: EventType
EventType.description: Ontology §6. Coarse routing categories, not a taxonomy of the world.

EvidenceTrailOut.title: EvidenceTrailOut
EvidenceTrailOut.description: A statement traced to the documents behind it (agent doc §2.4).

ExposureKind.title: ExposureKind
ExposureKind.description: Ontology §16 'Process Exposure' — how an Asset touches the Process.

quantitative_basis.title: Quantitative Basis
quantitative_basis.description: The figure a revenue share rests on, where one was supplied.

JournalEntryOut.title: JournalEntryOut
JournalEntryOut.description: Why the system changed its mind (PRD §21).

LogicOperator.title: LogicOperator
LogicOperator.description: Ontology §12 — Capability requirements form logical structures.

NodeRef.title: NodeRef
NodeRef.description: A pointer to any node, with enough to render it.

ProcessArchetype.title: ProcessArchetype
ProcessArchetype.description:
Ontology §8. Each archetype has its own State machine — see
``econiq_ontology.archetypes``.

ProcessStateLabel.title: ProcessStateLabel
ProcessStateLabel.description:
Every categorical State across all Archetypes.

A flat vocabulary keeps the database column typed; ``StateMachine`` enforces
which labels are legal for which Archetype.

transition_beliefs.title: Transition Beliefs
transition_beliefs.description: Model belief that the Process moves next to each State. Not probabilities: uncalibrated until the calibration framework validates them (ontology §35).

ProcessStatus.title: ProcessStatus
ProcessStatus.description:
Lifecycle of the Process object itself, distinct from its economic
State (ontology §7 vs §10).

raw.title: Raw
raw.description: The measurement, in its own units.

RankComponentOut.title: RankComponentOut
RankComponentOut.description:
One input to the Discover rank, with the arithmetic left visible.

Returned so the ranking can be taken apart on screen (#25). A rank nobody
can decompose is a number the reader has to take on trust, which is the
opposite of what this product is for.

RelationshipType.title: RelationshipType
RelationshipType.description:
Typed edges (ui_concept §9.1).

The canonical chain is::

    Process --influences--> Process
    Process --creates--> Bottleneck
    Bottleneck --requires--> Capability
    Capability --expressed_by--> Asset

Additional types carry evidence and direct Event exposure (ontology §15).

RequirementNodeOut.title: RequirementNodeOut
RequirementNodeOut.description:
One node of a requirement tree.

Returned as a tree rather than a flat list because AND and OR imply
completely different sets of participants (ontology §12), and flattening for
transport would discard the distinction the mapping agent was asked for.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: What the value was computed from.

ScoreFamily.title: ScoreFamily
ScoreFamily.description:
Ontology §17. These three are never collapsed into one number, anywhere.

Trade quality is V2 and is present only so that stored scores can never be
mislabelled; nothing in V1 produces it.

ScorecardOut.title: ScorecardOut
ScorecardOut.description:
One family, never a blend.

Thesis, Asset and Trade quality are separate by construction (ontology §17),
and there is deliberately no endpoint that combines them.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: 'measured' or 'estimated' — whether code computed it or an agent judged it.

occurred_at.title: Occurred At
occurred_at.description: When the thing being described happened.

subject_id.title: Subject Id
subject_id.description: The Event, State or entry this entry points at.

supports.title: Supports
supports.description: Evidence direction, where the entry is evidence.

TimelineEntryOut.title: TimelineEntryOut
TimelineEntryOut.description:
One dated thing that happened to a Process.

State changes, journal entries and evidence arrivals share an axis because
the question the Process screen answers is "what changed and why", and the
answer is usually an evidence arrival next to the belief change it caused.
Three separate lists would leave the reader doing that join by eye.

UnavailableInputOut.title: UnavailableInputOut
UnavailableInputOut.description: A §5.1 ranking input this deployment cannot compute, and why.
